Answer: B
Reason: Pulmonary aplasia is characterized by the complete absence of lung tissue and its associated vascular structures; therefore, the absence of the left pulmonary artery is the most specific finding distinguishing it from atelectasis or bronchiectasis, where the vessel would typically be present (though possibly displaced or diminished). The other findings (mediastinal shift, diaphragm elevation, rib crowding) are non-specific signs of volume loss common to all the listed differentials.
